full_judgment: 14. Thus it appears to us that the consideration of the statement under section 161 CrPC while passing an order framing charge or otherwise has not only been favoured but also taken as a necessary part of the duty cast upon the court and, therefore, use of the statement under section 161 CrPC in the instant case has not rendered the charge as groundless. Furthermore, from the reading of section 242 CrPC it is found that unlike passing an order of conviction the court has the option of discretion to make up his mind regarding the commission of an offence and such presumption could be derived from the perusal of the record of the case and documents connected therewith. Though the cases referred to above relate to the framing of the charge under the provision of section 250B CrPC we are of the view that the same principle is applicable to a case for framing charge under sections 241A and 242 which correspond to the provision of section 250B CrPC. On interpretation of sections 241A and 242 CrPC we find that the court has jurisdiction to pass an order of discharge if he is satisfied that the charge is groundless and if he finds so, he has to give reason but in framing charge it is not required for him to record reasons showing that there are grounds for framing charge, it is enough if the court is of the opinion that there is ground for presumption that the accused has committed the offence. The formation of such opinion is dependent only on the application of judicial mind based on materials collected from the record of the case. On perusal of the record and also impugned order dated 4.5.92 we do not find any basis to hold that the accused petitioner was taken by surprise, on the contrary, the record of the case shows that sufficient opportunity was given to the accused petitioner for making submission before the court while hearing the matter relating to the framing of the additional charge. Therefore, the contention of the learned Counsel for the accused that the petitioner was taken by surprise about framing of the additional/further charge does not appear to be of substance.
